title: What is canonical theology?
summary: Canonical theology reads the Bible as one ordered witness whose final form interprets its earlier parts in light of the whole.
historical_context: This approach grows from the church's long habit of reading Scripture as a unified canon rather than isolated fragments.
ancient_near_east_context: Ancient collections often guided interpretation by arrangement, and Scripture similarly invites readers to move from promise to fulfillment.
literary_context: Genesis, the Prophets, the Gospels, and the Epistles are read together so that the final shape of Scripture becomes part of its meaning.
covenantal_significance: Canonical theology protects continuity between the covenants while honoring the progressive unfolding of God's plan.
interpretive_notes: Read each passage in its own context, then in the larger canonical story.
Canonical theology is not flattening; it is disciplined synthesis around Christ.
common_questions: Why does the final shape of the Bible matter?
